previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was admitted for hypoxemia and increased oxygen requirements, found to have multifocal pneumonia on chest imaging. She had recently completed treatment for a UTI and reported a history of aspiration. Despite being afebrile and without leukocytosis, she required up to 12 liters of oxygen initially. Treatment with vancomycin and Zosyn was initiated due to prior MRSA and aspiration risk. She responded well, weaning to her baseline 2 liters within two days. Urine culture showed no growth, and Legionella antigen was negative. She remained stable, with plans for completion of an 8-day IV antibiotic course at home via PICC line. Discharge was arranged with home health support and follow-up with primary and pulmonary care.

Discharge Instructions:
Ms ___, 
You were admitted to the hospital because you had a desaturation 
to 85% at home on an increased amount of oxygen. We believe that 
this was caused by increased secretions in your airways, 
combined with your inability to cough up mucus. While you were 
here, we gave you Mucinex and performed chest ___ with an Acapela 
and a Flutter Vest. After that, you were able to cough up the 
secretions and your oxygen saturations remained in the 90% range 
on 3L of oxygen.
.
You will continue the vancomycin and Zosyn at home to treat the 
pneumonia. You should continue the Mucinex/Guiafenisin to help 
with the mucus. You might continue to require higher O2 while we 
treat the pneumonia, even up to ___ NC. Continuing chest ___ 
will be extremely important. This should be done manually, with 
the acapela/flutter valve, and with the vest. We will get in 
touch with respiratory equipment to get the vest machine 
delivered to your house. It is fine to check home O2 sats, but I 
would not get overly concerned about them as long as you are 
feeling well without shortness of breath or fast breathing. If 
the saturation is low, you will benefit from increasing the 
nasal cannula and clearing the mucus. With your lung disease, 
your O2 sat does not need to be higher than 90-91%. We will let 
Dr. ___ that he should make you an appointment for a 
sleep study in the future after you recover from your pneumonia. 
You should also make an appointment with your pulmonologist in 
the near future.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPHS

HISTORY:  Hypoxia.  Recent pneumonia.

COMPARISONS:  Prior day.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest, portable AP view.

FINDINGS:  A right-sided PICC line terminates at the cavoatrial junction.  The
heart is mild to moderately enlarged.  There is a similar opacity in the right
lower lung obscuring the right hemidiaphragm.  It is difficult to exclude
small pleural effusions, although there are no definite effusions. 
Superimposed on the prior process is prominent indistinct pulmonary
vascularity that is increased suggestive of a mild to moderate pulmonary
vascular congestion.  There is no pneumothorax.  Right-sided rib deformities
appear unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  Persistent right lower lung opacity worrisome for pneumonia. 
Superimposed diffuse but predominantly central opacification, which is not
entirely specific but most suggestive of pulmonary vascular congestion.
